name: Centro Historico
tagline: UNESCO colonial core, cathedrals and cobblestones
description: The historic heart of Cuenca, all red-tiled roofs, the blue-domed New Cathedral, and colonial plazas. Dense with cafes, restaurants, museums, and markets within easy walking distance. Lively during the day and around Parque Calderon, but some streets get quiet at night, so awareness matters after dark.
bestFor: first-time visitors, culture lovers, short-to-medium stays
pros: Walk to everything, plazas, museums, cafes
cons: Noisier, especially near plazas on weekends
Some pickpocketing risk in crowded areas

name: El Ejido
tagline: Leafy, central, popular with long-term expats
description: A residential district just south of the Tomebamba river, a short walk from the historic center. Known for tree-lined streets, riverside paths, and a strong concentration of long-term expats and remote workers. Good balance of quiet residential living and proximity to cafes and coworking-friendly spots.
pros: Quiet but close to the center
Good riverside walking and running paths
Solid apartment options with modern amenities
cons: Fewer late-night options than the center
Some streets have limited street lighting

name: Gringolandia (Av. Ordonez Lasso)
tagline: The expat corridor, familiar comforts and community
description: The stretch along Av. Ordonez Lasso northwest of the center has earned its nickname from the dense concentration of North American and European retirees and long-term expats. Expect English-friendly businesses, expat-oriented restaurants, and easy access to expat social groups, at a higher price point than most of the city.
bestFor: retirees, first-time expats wanting community, English speakers
pros: English widely spoken in shops and services
cons: Feels less locally Ecuadorian, more insular

name: Puertas del Sol / Yanuncay
tagline: Quiet residential area near the Yanuncay river
description: A calmer, more residential zone south of the center near the Yanuncay river, popular with locals and a growing number of value-conscious nomads. Offers lower rents than El Ejido or Gringolandia while still being within a manageable walk or short bus/tranvia ride to the historic core.
bestFor: budget-conscious long stays, those wanting a local feel
pros: More authentic, less touristed daily life
cons: Farther from nightlife and central cafes
